A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WYD benchmark, retaining 1,544 videos and nine annotation categories. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices A–E are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, category-level analyses, and human preference studies validating automatic metrics.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds VACE results, HumanVid comparisons, and experiments involving reconstruction and manually annotated poses.

M1.justification: The seven-step dataset curation procedure and mask-based pICD/pAPE approach are retained. Revised explanations, attribution to existing metrics, and experiments with additional models do not establish a change to the underlying proposed procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations on HumanVid's 71 videos and VACE scenarios using text-only or image-only inputs without pose guidance (Figs. 5–6). These extend evaluation coverage while retaining WYD's videos, source datasets, and categories.

E2.justification: VACE-Wan2.1 joins the pose comparisons and replaces TF-T2V in category-level comparisons. MagicAnimate and depth/edge models remain evaluated elsewhere. Metric validation adds an explicit pICD-versus-ICD comparison and drops PSNR; most existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 4 narrows the recommended six-metric suite to FVD, OFE, pICD, and pAPE, dropping standalone ICD and pFVD. New evaluation designs compare generation with autoencoder reconstruction, substitute pose detectors, and use manually annotated poses on 100 videos. The existing 16-fps setting and Appendix D human-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial controls testing reconstruction capacity, OpenPose versus DWPose, and sensitivity to pose errors using manual annotations (Figs. 44–46), plus VACE modality ablations (Fig. 6). Earlier category analyses remain with revised model membership. The separate pFVD/pJEDi and frame-similarity metric comparisons are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated generation runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. Human validation retains the same sampling and reporting practices, including rank correlation and pairwise accuracy.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical and qualitative results for VACE, HumanVid, and the new controls. For example, text-conditioned VACE reports FVD 276, pICD 19, and pAPE 47 in Fig. 4. Table 2 changes the attribution of 72.67% agreement from ICD to pICD, reports ICD at 67.33%, and removes the PSNR and VMAF agreement entries.

T1.justification: Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs. The retained metric definitions, including pAPE as the complement of mean pose AP, are explained and attributed differently without an established substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly claims new metrics, particularly pAPE, as a distinct contribution. v2 instead presents the metrics as adaptations of existing subject-consistency and pose-AP measures, materially narrowing the methodological novelty claim. The central claims about WYD's diversity, difficulty, and diagnostic value remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new controls as evidence that generation, rather than reconstruction capacity or pose-detector choice, drives the observed difficulties. It adds a size-dependent tradeoff between pose adherence and visual detail. Existing distribution-shift and disappearing-object limitations remain, while the explicit limitation concerning face and emotion assessment is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 documents the manual pose-annotation workflow and interface, expands model training-data disclosures, and revises reported annotation effort and computation from over 5,000 to over 6,000 A100 GPU hours. It omits v1's explicit description of autoregressive extension for short-video models. These documentation changes do not establish changes to retained experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises metric positioning by acknowledging prior pose-AP use and crediting ConsistI2V for the consistency-metric inspiration. Related work expands discussion of HumanVid and reference-video requirements, and introduces works including AIGCBench, T2V-CompBench, and VACE while removing numerous earlier background citations.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, evaluation discussion, and diagnostic narrative are extensively rewritten. Detailed filtering and categorization descriptions move into Appendix B, the main method description is condensed, and limitations are incorporated into the conclusion. These are substantial structural changes beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, adds a metric schematic and several experimental plots, separates pose results from appendix depth/edge results, and adds VACE rows to existing qualitative grids. Category plots are redrawn, tables are restructured, and the pose-annotation interface is added; several older metric plots disappear.

improvement.justification: The reconstruction and pose controls address important alternative explanations absent from v1, while the revised novelty attribution improves scientific positioning. However, reporting inconsistencies temper these gains: Table 2 reassigns 72.67% from ICD to pICD without explanation, and Fig. 47's FVD-labeled actor-count trend conflicts with Fig. 7 and the accompanying interpretation. The added validation supports a positive but limited net improvement.
